cond_0001.intro:
[Company name masked] is looking to add a Senior Engineer to its Generation Asset Management team. The Senior Engineer is an experienced engineer that drives the safe and reliable operation the District's electrical generating assets. The individual is assigned accountability for specific engineering and asset management programs and provides timely technical analyses on plant equipment and systems, and operating and maintenance practices, in order to ensure economic and technically sound operations. Position is primarily based centrally at the corporate headquarters but may be called upon to serve on-site at any of the generating stations. Works closely with [Company name masked] generation facility staff, other departments within [Company name masked], outside vendors, and/or contractors to acquire information, resolve problems and implement solutions.
Generation Asset Management is responsible for 3 general functions to support operation of [Company name masked]'s generation assets. This engineering role will primarily work in 1 of these functional areas but also support the other areas when needed. Those areas are as follows:
Engineering Programs (i.e. Boiler reliability, welding, high energy piping, etc)
Long Term Asset Management (e.g. Developing Asset Management Plans)
Predictive Maintenance (PdM) and Rotating Equipment Subject Matter Experts
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
4-Year BS Engineering degree (ABET-accredited)
Five (5) years of equivalent engineering work experience (Master's degree may be considered for up to two years of experience)
Professional Engineer (PE) certificate, NERC, or other approved job-related certification; PE certificate or means for reciprocity within six months
Demonstrated ability to perform complex engineering tasks and intricate studies as well as present the results
Demonstrated effective analytical, problem solving and decision making abilities utilizing creativity, foresight and mature judgement
Strong communications, presentation, and negotiation skills
Strong understanding of power plant system design, operation, maintenance and system interactions
Demonstrated ability to work as part of a team, exercise flexibility and take responsibility for assigned work
Understanding and application of applicable industry standards and codes of construction: ASME, OSHA, NFPA, etc.
Possess and maintain a valid driver's license
Demonstrated capabilities in multiple aspects of equipment reliability and diagnostics (PdM Only)
Category III or higher certification in vibration analysis or within 2 years of employment (PdM Only)
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity and experience with [Product name masked], Maximo, [Product name masked], AutoDesk (CAD, Inventor, Vault), Bentley MicroStation, [Product name masked], SharePoint
Familiarity and experience with [Product name masked], [Product name masked], [Product name masked], and SharePoint
Familiarity and experience with Tableau or Power BI
Advanced User MS Office Professional Skills (e.g. Pivot tables, data links, SQL, etc)
Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification
Knowledge base in specific assigned program: reliability, efficiency, boiler, welding, operating statistics, etc
Advanced Degree (MS or MBA)
Masters, minor, or certificate program level education in data analytics, mathematical modeling, or management information systems
Experience consolidating and interpreting multiple data sources to determine an optimized solution
Working knowledge of ISO 55000
Applicable qualifications or certificates from Institute of Asset Management or equivalent professional body
Supervisory, Leadership, or Management experience
Strong knowledge base in power plant programs
Strong knowledge base in Predictive Maintenance
Thorough knowledge of generating stations and energy markets
FAA Part 107 Certification for Remote Pilot of unmanned aircraft
Category IV vibration analyst certification (PdM specific)
Experience balancing rotating equipment (PdM specific)
Certification or training in any of the following: Lubrication Analysis, Motor Offline/Online Motor Testing, Infrared Thermography (PdM specific)

The Senior Engineer is an experienced engineer responsible for the safe and reliable operation of the District's electrical generating assets. The individual is assigned accountability for specific engineering and asset management programs and provides timely technical analyses on plant equipment and systems, and operating and maintenance practices, to ensure economic and technically sound operations. The position is primarily based at the corporate headquarters at [Location masked] but may be required to serve on-site at any of the generating stations. The role involves coordination with [Company name masked] generation facility staff, other internal departments, outside vendors, and contractors to gather information, resolve problems, and implement solutions.
Generation Asset Management covers 3 general functions to support operation of [Company name masked]'s generation assets. This engineering role will primarily work in 1 of these functional areas but also support the other areas when needed. Those areas are as follows:
Engineering Programs (i.e. Boiler reliability, welding, high energy piping, etc)
Long Term Asset Management (e.g. Developing Asset Management Plans)
Predictive Maintenance (PdM) and Rotating Equipment Subject Matter Experts
cond_0196.responsibilities:
Provide technical analyses on plant equipment and systems, operating practices, and maintenance practices to support sound and economic operations.
Take accountability for assigned engineering and asset management programs.
Coordinate with generation facility staff, internal departments, vendors, and contractors on specific tasks to gather information, resolve problems, and implement solutions.
Support one primary functional area within Generation Asset Management while providing input to the other areas as project needs require.
Conduct engineering studies and document findings for sharing with relevant stakeholders.
Apply industry standards and codes (ASME, OSHA, NFPA, etc.) to assigned work.
Contribute technical input to long-term asset management planning efforts.
Perform equipment reliability and diagnostic work within assigned program scope (PdM roles).
Carry out on-site work at generating stations when required.
cond_0196.requirements:
4-Year BS Engineering degree (ABET-accredited)

The Senior Engineer is an experienced engineer that drives the safe and reliable operation of the District's electrical generating assets. The individual is assigned accountability for specific engineering and asset management programs and delivers timely technical analyses on plant equipment and systems, and operating and maintenance practices, to ensure economic and technically sound operations. cond_0556.intro:
[Company name masked] is looking to add a Senior Engineer to its Generation Asset Management team. The Senior Engineer is an experienced engineer responsible for the safe and reliable operation of the District's electrical generating assets. The individual is assigned accountability for specific engineering and asset management programs and provides timely technical analyses on plant equipment and systems, and operating and maintenance practices, to ensure economic and technically sound operations. The position is primarily based at the corporate headquarters at [Location masked] but may be required to serve on-site at any of the generating stations. The role involves coordination with [Company name masked] generation facility staff, other internal departments, outside vendors, and contractors to gather information, resolve problems, and implement solutions.
Generation Asset Management covers 3 general functions to support operation of [Company name masked]'s generation assets. This engineering role will primarily work in 1 of these functional areas but also support the other areas when needed. Those areas are as follows:
Engineering Programs (i.e. Boiler reliability, welding, high energy piping, etc)
Long Term Asset Management (e.g. Developing Asset Management Plans)
Predictive Maintenance (PdM) and Rotating Equipment Subject Matter Experts
cond_0556.responsibilities:
Provide technical analyses on plant equipment and systems, operating practices, and maintenance practices to support sound and economic operations.
Take accountability for assigned engineering and asset management programs.
Coordinate with generation facility staff, internal departments, vendors, and contractors on specific tasks to gather information, resolve problems, and implement solutions.
Support one primary functional area within Generation Asset Management while providing input to the other areas as project needs require.
Conduct engineering studies and document findings for sharing with relevant stakeholders.
Apply industry standards and codes (ASME, OSHA, NFPA, etc.) to assigned work.
Contribute technical input to long-term asset management planning efforts.
Perform equipment reliability and diagnostic work within assigned program scope (PdM roles).
Carry out on-site work at generating stations when required.
